notes.why: The polite -თ ending: drivers say it to every passenger.
From მოსვლა, to come.

lines.en: Come in! What would you like?
That's expensive. Could you take a little off?
All right, I'll let you have it for three lari.

notes.why: Fruit and vegetables are often named in the singular: პომიდორი, "tomato".
Said when handing something over.

lines.ka: მადლობა. ხორცს არ ვჭამ. რას მირჩევთ?
lines.lat: madloba. khortss ar vch'am. ras mirchevt?
lines.en: Thanks. I don't eat meat. What do you recommend?
Aubergine with walnuts, and Adjarian khachapuri.
Is there meat in the lobio?
No, the lobio has no meat.

lines.ka: მაშინ ლობიო და ერთი ხაჭაპური, თუ შეიძლება.
lines.lat: mashin lobio da erti khach'ap'uri, tu sheidzleba.
lines.en: Then the lobio and one khachapuri, please.
What would you like to drink?

notes.why: უ- … -ო makes "without": უგაზო, without gas (still).
A very polite word waiters use.

lines.en: For here or to take away?
No, thanks. How much is it?

notes.why: Literally "for taking away".

lines.en: Hello. Do you have something for a headache?
Yes. You don't have any allergies, do you?
No, I don't. How many times a day?

notes.why: ხომ turns a sentence into a check, like "…, do you?"

lines.en: Hello, I'd like to book an appointment with a doctor.
I have a sore throat and a fever.
Can you come tomorrow at eleven?
Yes. Do you have a doctor who speaks English?

notes.why: Literally "I'm listening to you": how offices answer.
Literally "what is bothering you?": what doctors ask.

lines.en: Thank you. My name is John.
I'm Nana. Where are you from?
Well done! If you need anything, tell me.
Thank you very much, very nice to meet you.

notes.why: A warm, formal welcome.
Georgians love to hear a foreigner try their language.

lines.ka: გამარჯობა, ბატონო გიორგი. ცხელი წყალი არ მოდის.
lines.lat: gamarjoba, bat'ono giorgi. tskheli ts'q'ali ar modis.
lines.en: Hello, Mr Giorgi. There's no hot water.
Oh, sorry. Is the boiler on?
At ten in the morning. Will you be at home?
Yes, I'll be at home. Thank you.

notes.why: Before a first name: ბატონო გიორგი. For a woman: ქალბატონო ნანა.

lines.en: Hello! How can I help you?

lines.ka: თვიური ასი ლარია, ერთჯერადი ვიზიტი თხუთმეტი.
lines.lat: tviuri asi laria, ertjeradi vizit'i tkhutmet'i.
lines.en: A month is a hundred lari, a single visit fifteen.
I'd like a monthly one. Do you have personal trainers too?
On the right. The towels are here.

notes.why: For people and animals Georgian uses ყავს instead of აქვს.

lines.en: Excuse me, where is the metro?
Go straight on, then turn left.
No, it's five minutes on foot.

lines.ka: ბოდიში, ვერ გავიგე. გაიმეორეთ, თუ შეიძლება.
lines.lat: bodishi, ver gavige. gaimeoret, tu sheidzleba.
lines.en: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you repeat it?

notes.why: Everyday "then, after that".

lines.en: Hello, I have a room booked.
Here you are. Is breakfast included?

notes.why: -დან is from, -მდე is up to.

lines.en: Hello, I'd like a SIM card.

lines.ka: კი, აი. ინტერნეტის პაკეტი რა ღირს?
lines.lat: k'i, ai. int'ernet'is p'ak'et'i ra ghirs?
lines.en: Yes, here. How much is an internet package?

notes.why: Future of აღება, to take: the way to say yes to a price.

lines.en: There's been an accident. Someone is hurt.
On Chavchavadze Avenue, by the university.
An ambulance is coming. Stay where you are.

notes.why: Say where you are first: the street, and something near it.
If Georgian fails you, ask: ინგლისური იცით?

lines.en: Hello! How can I help you?

lines.ka: გამარჯობა. ეს ამანათი პოლონეთში უნდა გავაგზავნო.
lines.lat: gamarjoba. es amanati p'olonetshi unda gavagzavno.
lines.en: Hello. I need to send this parcel to Poland.

lines.ka: აქ დადეთ, თუ შეიძლება. რა არის შიგნით?
lines.lat: ak dadet, tu sheidzleba. ra aris shignit?
lines.en: Put it here, please. What's inside?
Standard. How long will it take?
OK. Can I pay by card?

notes.why: -ში means both in and into: პოლონეთში, in Poland or to Poland.
უნდა + a verb: "I have to", "I need to".

lines.en: A little shorter, here and here.

lines.ka: კი. ზემოთ მხოლოდ ცოტა, თუ შეიძლება.
lines.lat: k'i. zemot mkholod tsot'a, tu sheidzleba.
lines.en: Yes. Only a little on top, please.
OK. Shall I wash your hair?
No, thanks. How much is it?
I really like it, thank you very much!

notes.why: Very polite. It can also mean "come in" or "welcome".
Literally "the cutting of hair": თმა is hair.

lines.en: Hello. I'd like to change some euros.
Here you are. The receipt is here too.
Thank you. Where is the cash machine?
By the entrance, on the right.

notes.why: From ფულის გადაცვლა, changing money.
-ც on the end of a word means "too, also".

lines.en: Excuse me, does this marshrutka go to Vake?
Yes, it does. Have a seat.

lines.ka: როცა ჭავჭავაძეზე მივალთ, მითხარით, თუ შეიძლება.
lines.lat: rotsa ch'avch'avadzeze mivalt, mitkharit, tu sheidzleba.
lines.en: Please tell me when we get to Chavchavadze.

notes.why: მი- puts "me" in the verb, and -თ makes it polite.
გ- is "you", as in გინდა.

lines.en: Come in, come in! How are you?
Fine, thanks. This is for you.
You shouldn't have! Sit down, help yourself.
This is delicious! What is it?
Shall I pour you some wine?
Cheers! Thank you so much for your hospitality.

notes.why: A warm, polite word for "eat", said to guests.
"Victory to…": the toast. What you drink to comes first: შენი ჯანმრთელობის გაუმარჯოს.

lines.en: Hello! Can I help you with anything?

lines.ka: ეს მაისური მომწონს. უფრო დიდი ზომა გაქვთ?
lines.lat: es maisuri momts'ons. upro didi zoma gakvt?
lines.en: I like this T-shirt. Do you have a bigger size?

lines.ka: კი, აი. მოზომეთ, გასახდელი იქ არის.
lines.lat: k'i, ai. mozomet, gasakhdeli ik aris.
lines.en: Yes, here. Try it on, the fitting room is over there.
It fits well. How much is it?
Thirty lari. There's a sale on now.
I'll take it. Can I pay by card?

notes.why: მ- for "me" again, as in მინდა and მომწონს.
ფასი (price) + დაკლება (taking off).

lines.en: Hello! Does this path go to the lake?
Yes, go straight on, as far as the bridge.
How many hours is it on foot?
Is there a spring on the way?
Yes, after the bridge. The water is clean.
What will the weather be like?
It may rain in the evening. Come back early.

notes.why: -მდე: up to, as far as.
შეიძლება also means "maybe, it may".

lines.en: OK, let's make it a bit lighter.
That's better. Can I take a break?
Rest for a minute, then we'll carry on.

notes.why: Also "repeating": გაიმეორეთ, please repeat.
To a friend; politely: დაისვენეთ.
